predecessors.note: Only the Sredny Stog has a dossier; its own page ends it c. 3500 BC, a century before the Yamnaya core of 3400 BC and three before the spread to the Dnieper (3200 BC), so the Dnieper-Donets steppe is nobody's land in between (notes).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives the infobox start as c. 3300 BC but the origin 'at c. 3400 BC' in the Don-Volga area (Anthony) and the early-Yamnaya map caption at 3400 BC; the core is drawn from 3400 as Rostov, Volgograd and Kalmykia, the stand-in for the Don-Volga area. No area figure on the page to compare; the core is about 0.28 M km2 in the gazetteer.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The steppe from the Southern Bug and Dniester to the Ural after the 3400-3200 BC spread: the gazetteer's Pontic Steppe plus Saratov, Samara, Orenburg and West Kazakhstan for the Volga-Ural side, minus the Odessa and Kirovohrad oblasts (228 cells, about 58,000 km2), which cucuteni-trypillia-culture draws until its 3000 BCE end; the Yamnaya takes them in 3000 BCE (ledger). The page says the spread reached the "Southern Bug, Dniester" region in general; it does not say that these two oblasts were Yamnaya before the Cucuteni ended. The page gives no area; the drawn shape is about 1.06 M km2 in the gazetteer.

correction.text: "the region between the Southern Bug, Dniester, and Ural rivers" (the Pontic–Caspian steppe); infobox range "Pontic–Caspian steppe in Europe"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: from 3000 BCE the Yamnaya also holds the Odessa and Kirovohrad oblasts, which the Cucuteni-Trypillia culture holds to its end (infobox "c. 4800 to 3000 BC"; "the third wave of Kurgan expansion between 3000-2800 BC"). The Yamnaya page lists Cucuteni-Trypillia under "Preceded by" without a date. The page gives no area; the drawn shape is about 1.12 M km2 in the gazetteer.

region.text: "originated in the Don–Volga area at c. 3400 BC" (Anthony 2007); map caption "Early Yamnaya culture (3400 BC), according to Anthony (2007)"

ledger.note: 3400: the Yamnaya culture arises in the Don-Volga steppe. The page: Anthony "suggested that the Yamnaya culture (3300–2600 BC) originated in the Don–Volga area at c. 3400 BC"; the Mykhailivka culture "formed the core Yamnaya culture (c. 3600–3400 BC)" on the lower Dnieper; the Repin culture (c. 3950–3300 BC) and the Khvalynsk culture (4700–3800 BC) precede it, none drawn. [Reviewer xx-01-a, 2026-10-18: confidence 3 to 2: the infobox starts the culture c. 3300 BC against Anthony's c. 3400 BC, and Rostov/Volgograd/Kalmykia stand in for the page's "Don-Volga area"]

minus.text: the Don-Volga core and the Odessa and Kirovohrad oblasts

region.text: "the early Yamnaya horizon spread quickly across the Pontic–Caspian steppes between c. 3400 and 3200 BC"

ledger.note: 3200: the early Yamnaya horizon has spread across the Pontic-Caspian steppe. The page: Anthony "argues that the early Yamnaya horizon spread quickly across the Pontic–Caspian steppes between c. 3400 and 3200 BC"; the year 3200 is the end of that span. The land was the Sredny Stog's (to c. 3500 BC), the Usatovo's (c. 3500–3000 BC) and others', none with a live dossier. The Odessa and Kirovohrad oblasts are left out: cucuteni-trypillia-culture holds them to 3000 BCE and the Yamnaya takes them then.

region.text: the Odessa and Kirovohrad oblasts, the Cucuteni-Trypillia culture's land on the Southern Bug and Dnieper bend until 3000 BCE

ledger.note: 3000 BCE: the Odessa and Kirovohrad oblasts pass from the Cucuteni-Trypillia culture to the Yamnaya. The Cucuteni-Trypillia page: infobox "c. 4800 to 3000 BC", "the third wave of Kurgan expansion between 3000-2800 BC", "the Yamnaya culture (3300-2600 BC)"; the Yamnaya page lists Cucuteni-Trypillia under "Preceded by". The year is the page's end of the Cucuteni-Trypillia culture; the page names neither oblast (the region is the Cucuteni dossier's reading of the "Dnieper and Southern Bug" extent), so confidence 2.

region.text: "the region between the Southern Bug, Dniester, and Ural rivers" (the Pontic–Caspian steppe); infobox range "Pontic–Caspian steppe in Europe"

ledger.note: 2600: the Yamnaya culture gives way to the Catacomb culture in the west and the Poltavka culture in the east. The page: infobox "c. 3300–2600 BC", and "succeeded in its western range by the Catacomb culture (2800–2200 BC)" and in the eastern range by the Poltavka (2700–2100 BC); those starts are earlier than the Yamnaya end, so the successors overlap its last two centuries (the Catacomb page says ca. 2500–1950 BC, the Poltavka page c. 2800 BC). Poltavka is the second counterpart (east of the Volga); no boundary between the ranges is given.

certainty.note: A steppe culture drawn by modern oblasts and a gazetteer region; every edge is soft, and the page gives no boundary except the three rivers of its lead.

notes:
Culture dossier (the brief's 'early Yamnaya on the steppe'), from three pages, written after the earlier run of this batch reported it unreached. It begins after the group's 3400 BCE horizon and runs to 2600 BCE so the steppe is never blank. Disagreements: start 3300 BC (infobox) vs c. 3400 BC (Anthony, map caption) vs a core formed 3600-3400 BC (Mykhailivka); 3400 is used and the first keyframe is the Don-Volga core only. End 2600 BC (lead) vs 2500 BC (the origin paragraph). Catacomb 2800-2200 BC (Yamnaya page) vs ca. 2500-1950 BC (Catacomb page); Poltavka 2700-2100 BC (Yamnaya page) vs c. 2800-2100 BC (Poltavka page): the hand-over is drawn at the Yamnaya end, 2600. Cross-dossier: sredny-stog-culture dissolves in 3500 BCE naming yamnaya-culture as heir, a century before this dossier starts and three before the Yamnaya reaches the Dnieper, so the Dnieper-Donets steppe is blank 3500..3201 BCE; a fix is to end the Sredny Stog at 3200 or hand its land to nobody. No area figure on any of the three pages. The Corded Ware (north, undated on the page), the Afanasievo (Altai, migration undated), Vucedol, Repin, Khvalynsk, Mykhailivka and Usatovo have no dossier; the westward Danube-Hungary reach is not dated on the page and not drawn. Gazetteer: 'Don-Volga area' and 'Volga-Ural steppe' are not regions (admin1 lists stand in); the Pontic Steppe region includes Krasnodar and Stavropol, which the page does not name.

Repair 2026-10-18 (after the reviewer): the Odessa and Kirovohrad oblasts (228 cells) are no longer drawn from 3200 BCE: cucuteni-trypillia-culture holds them to its end in 3000 BCE (its infobox 'c. 4800 to 3000 BC'), so keyframe 1 ends 3001 BCE without them, ledger 1 (3200) leaves them out, and a new keyframe yamnaya-culture_-3000 and a gain in 3000 BCE (counterpart cucuteni-trypillia-culture, confidence 2) bring them in; cucuteni-trypillia-culture is added to identity.predecessors with that land. Doubt: the Yamnaya page says the early horizon 'spread quickly across the Pontic-Caspian steppes between c. 3400 and 3200 BC' and its lead puts the range between the Southern Bug, Dniester and Ural, which would favour a Yamnaya presence in those oblasts before 3000; the page says nothing specific of Odessa or Kirovohrad (Usatovo, c. 3500-3000 BC on its map caption, has no dossier), and the Cucuteni page names neither oblast, so the choice between 3200 and 3000 is a reading either way; I followed the reviewer in using the other dossier's end year to avoid drawing the same land twice. The Cucuteni-Trypillia page was re-read for this fix: infobox 'c. 4800 to 3000 BC', lead 'c. 5050 to 2950 BC', 'the third wave of Kurgan expansion between 3000-2800 BC', Yamnaya '(3300-2600 BC)'. The drawn area of keyframe 1 is about 1.06 M km2 (was 1.12). Confidence of ledger 0 (start 3400) stays at the reviewer's 2.
